manifest.name: HANDS Visual Studio
manifest.summary: Editable element-level video projects with independent transparent figures, graphics, text, audio and motion; local HANDS timeline.
manifest.author: HANDS for GPT

instructions: Use HANDS Visual Studio with separate atomic elements, never only a final MP4. For every NEW video, first author scenegraph.json with stable unique element IDs and one independently editable layer per visible object: background, actor, prop, light, label, camera-facing overlay, audio. Compile with hands_scenegraph.py into a visual-studio.json plus elements/*.svg and transparent elements/*.png. Save scenegraph.json and code source, and edit the original objects through HANDS Visual Studio instead of only cutting scenes. Each layer supports start, duration, x/y, width/height, track, opacity, rotation, fades, and motion.toX/toY. For video/3D animations supply an isolated transparent source pass per object (ProRes 4444 with alpha when supported), or preserve the originating source scene graph and transform props. Flat MP4 imports can only be edited clip-by-clip. For existing ReelMade and Episode Studio generators, use scenegraph.json as a companion source contract, so their render scripts compile atomic layers automatically when present. Never render a separate flattened background containing visible objects that are also re-added as editable layers.

recipes.title: Open and edit a HANDS video

steps.instruction: Open HANDS Tools > HANDS Visual Studio, pin it, then select it from the left sidebar.
Select a project or import a generated project folder and inspect its layers.
Move and resize layers, adjust starts/durations, trim audio, update text and save the .hvs.json revision.
Export an MP4 and review it while keeping all source and project files.
Generate original video with Remotion Director or ReelMade, preserving source code, media assets and timeline metadata.
Write visual-studio.json with individual source layers, independent audio files, start/duration/track plus viewport coordinates.
Import the project in HANDS Visual Studio; preserve manual edits when changing the generation code.
List every visible object and sound, assign unique stable element IDs and preserve code/3D source.
Author scenegraph.json and source transparent vector/image/video layers with independent layout, timing, and animation.
Compile with python3 hands_scenegraph.py PROJECT_FOLDER and import visual-studio.json in HANDS.
Edit one object visually, save the revision, export H.264, and verify the rest of the elements remain unchanged.
